to a record_request and the attachment arrived through that channel.
Worth being deliberate: the same email content could arrive either way, and the

_why_this_document_matters: It is the exact inverse of the Doc Side invoice. The invoice states
administration dates and no expiries; this states expiries and no administration
dates. Both produce zero vaccination records, for opposite reasons.
Together they produce two complete records. That pairing is the most important
thing in the corpus and the schema currently has no honest way to express it.

line_items.term: Fecal Cent. & Giardia to Antech T808

_administered_on_is_null_on_every_row: The mirror image of the invoice. Seven rows, seven expiry dates, not one
administration date. vaccination_record.administered_on is date NOT NULL, so
this document creates nothing either — for the opposite reason.
The README tells the no-expiry story. This is an equally good no-administration
-date story that it does not tell, and the pair is more persuasive than either.
_two_rows_one_combination_shot: Rows 1 and 4 both name DHPP and Leptospira. They are not duplicates and they
are not one row that maps to two vaccines — they are two products with two
durations, cross-referencing each other in their names:
'DHPP 3YR W/ LEPTO'          expiry 2028-04-03  -> the 3-year DHPP component
'Leptospira 4x Annual w/ DHPP' expiry 2027-04-02 -> the 1-year lepto component
The invoice confirms it: on 2025-04-04 the clinic billed 'DHPP 3YR' and
'Leptospira 4x Annual' as two separate items at two prices. Each email row maps
to exactly ONE vaccine — the one whose duration its expiry reflects.
This corrects an earlier assumption that a compound term implies one line to
many vaccines. Here it is the reverse: the compound naming is a cross-reference,
and mapping either row to both vaccines would create four records from two
shots, two of them with the wrong expiry.
_line_item_notes._status_column: Six Active, one Expired, computed by the clinic against its own report date. Transcribed into status_raw and used for nothing. See must_not_produce[3] and [4].

The From address belongs to a sending platform, not the clinic. See must_not_produce[6].

must_not_produce.why_tempting: 'Active' sounds like a confirmation, and verification_status has a value that sounds like it means the same thing.
must_not_produce._note: verification_status records whether a HUMAN AT THE SHOP checked the record against the document. The clinic's Status column is another system's computation about currency, not about verification, and mapping one to the other would let an email mark itself verified. verification_coherent would then also demand verified_by and verified_at, which the page cannot supply.

must_not_produce.why_tempting: The clinic has already done the computation and it agrees with what the system would conclude — for the vaccines this clinic knows about.
must_not_produce._note: It does not know about the BetterVet rabies dose, and it applies its own thresholds and its own report date. compliance_state is computed at read time from records the shop holds, which is the point of computing it at read time.

must_not_produce._note: owner.email is what the shop would use to send a record request. Taking the delivery address of a forwarded message is how a request silently goes nowhere. Both are real; the client record is the one that answers 'how does the practice reach this person'.

resolution._layer: 2 — the database interprets what the model transcribed. Not part of the model's score.

line_items._reasoning: Maps to DHPP alone, not to DHPP and leptospirosis. The 2028 expiry is a three-year interval, which is the DHPP component's duration; the lepto component is row 4 with its own one-year expiry. Confirmed by the invoice billing the two as separate items on 2025-04-04. Medium confidence because it depends on that cross-document check, and a reader with only this page could reasonably map it both ways.

'Rabies Vaccine 3 Yr Canine' — a fourth spelling of the same term, after BetterVet's 'Rabies Vaccine - 1 year', Petly's 'Rabies Vaccine 3 Year' and the invoice's 'Rabies Vaccination 3 Yr.'. Cadence, species and the vaccine/vaccination alternation all normalise away.
Maps to leptospirosis alone. The 2027-04-02 expiry is a one-year interval from an April 2026 dose — the lepto duration, not DHPP's.

A test panel, and the third distinct spelling of it in the corpus after Petly's four separate rows and the invoice's 'Heartworm, E.Canis & Lyme Test'. Vendor and catalogue codes in the term must normalise away.

cross_document: Both differences are exactly three years minus one day, which confirms the
clinic's expiry convention and confirms the two documents describe the same two
Bordetella and leptospirosis do NOT pair. Their 2027-04-02 expiries imply a dose
around 2026-04-03, from a visit neither document records. Two of the four
vaccines are still incomplete even with both pages in hand — which is a useful
corrective to the idea that one more document always closes the gap.
notes: The easiest document in the corpus to read and one of the two hardest to use. Clean HTML table, unambiguous dates, no OCR — and it produces nothing.
Four documents, four spellings of 'rabies'. That single term is the best argument in the corpus for a vocabulary table maintained as data rather than synonyms enumerated in a prompt.

Row 1 and row 4 corrected an assumption I had recorded earlier in the Petly key — that a compound term like 'DHPP 3YR W/ LEPTO' implies one line mapping to two vaccines. The invoice's separate billing lines show the opposite. Left visible rather than quietly fixed, because the labelling pass finding it is the argument for doing a labelling pass.
